headline: 🔥 PHONE LINES JAMMED — DITTOHEADS DROWNING OUT THE RIVAL HOST
factoid: Limbaugh's audience famously coordinated rapid call-in waves to influence other programs and consumer-feedback lines. The 1992 'Operation Chaos' (a Limbaugh-organised effort to influence the Democratic primary) was one of the earliest deliberate uses of an aligned audience as a strategic political weapon.

headline: 🔥 KILLED STORY RESURFACES — DRUDGE POSTS WHAT NEWSWEEK SHELVED
factoid: Drudge's January 1998 Lewinsky scoop (after Newsweek shelved Michael Isikoff's article) was the proof-of-concept moment for the 'aggregator as upstream editor' pattern. By 2007, Politico's analysis tracked roughly two-thirds of Drudge lead links migrating to cable news within 24 hours.

headline: 🔥 33 MILLION VOTER GUIDES IN CHURCH PEWS BY SUNDAY MORNING
factoid: The Christian Coalition distributed 33 million voter guides in churches on the Sunday before the 1992 election and 45 million for 1996. The IRS revoked the organization's 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status in 1999, ruling the guides insufficiently nonpartisan — but the model had already institutionalised across thousands of churches.

headline: 🔥 CABLE CHYRON STAYS UP 14 HOURS — STORY OUTLIVES ITS RETRACTION
factoid: Cable-news lower-third chyrons (the on-screen text strip) became a distinct editorial channel during the 2000s — often advancing narratives the anchor's spoken script did not. Network producers operate the chyron with no fact-check obligation tied to the anchor's spoken content.

headline: 🔥 GINGRICH'S WORD LIST CIRCULATES — EVERY GOP CANDIDATE SAYS 'PATHETIC'
factoid: Newt Gingrich's 1990 GOPAC training memo 'Language: A Key Mechanism of Control' instructed Republican candidates to use 64 specific words about opponents and 64 about themselves. The leaked memo became one of the most-cited documents in U.S. partisan vocabulary engineering.

headline: ⚡ FRENZY: DITTOHEADS FLOOD THE LINES — EVERY HOST RUNNING YOUR SCRIPT
factoid: By 1993, talk radio reached ~50% of U.S. adults weekly. AM stations could coordinate audience response within hours — listener call-in waves, congressional-office phone-line floods, and letter-writing campaigns were a documented organising layer years before the internet enabled the same dynamics digitally.
